social_circle.name: Hyejin Choi

demographics.occupation: Part-time counter worker and cake decorator at a small Korean bakery in Diamond Bar

background.how_they_met: Yasuko's mother; raised her in Pomona and then in a small Rowland Heights apartment after the 2007 divorce.
background.why_close: Sole custodial parent from age 13 onward; weekly Sunday dinners and near-daily contact have continued into adulthood. Hyejin's fall-2025 ER scare tightened the bond and increased Yasuko's check-in cadence.

interests: baking (red bean buns, soboro, first-birthday cakes)
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Mix of Korean and English texts, often short and functional with no punctuation. Frequent voice notes when something with her car or phone confuses her. Sends photos of food and the Korean drama she's watching. Uses Kakao stickers occasionally; rarely uses emoji.

shared_activities: Sunday dinner in Diamond Bar with banchan and a Korean drama
Translating new car noises over the phone
Obon and Chuseok observances
Driving her to follow-up medical appointments since the fall-2025 ER trip
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily or near-daily (mix of texts and calls)
recent_text_topics: A new rattling sound from under her Camry that she wants Yasuko to diagnose before her next bakery shift.
Pushing Yasuko to come for Sunday dinner more reliably; reporting which banchan she's already prepped.
Mild updates from her cardiology follow-up and whether she remembered to take the omeprazole.
Forwarded photos of cakes she decorated that day, plus the occasional 'when are you getting married' nudge framed as a joke.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'My mom, Hyejin, lives in Diamond Bar — she's sixty-two, still works part time at a Korean bakery. We talk every couple of days, and I drive over for dinner most Sundays.' Q17: 'I check in on my mom every couple days, partly because her car is always making a new sound she needs translated.' Q35: mother's fall-2025 ER scare. Q104: Diamond Bar Korean bakery, 15 years.

social_circle.name: Daichi Choi

demographics.occupation: Logistics coordinator at the Port of Long Beach
demographics.education: Some college (community college coursework, no degree)

background.how_they_met: Siblings; lived together with their mother in Rowland Heights after the divorce.
background.why_close: Survived their parents' divorce and the tight Rowland Heights years together; quietly close in adulthood — share a Spotify family plan and a 'deep distrust of group chats.' He's the practical counterweight who nags her about retirement saving and was the one who pushed her to open the Roth IRA.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Mostly memes, screenshots, and one-line zingers. Texts in lowercase, almost never uses punctuation. Switches to longer messages only when nagging her about money or venting about a Long Beach traffic stop.

shared_activities: Monthly ramen meetups
Shared Spotify family plan and trading playlist adds
Sunday dinners at mom's when he's willing to make the drive
Occasional overnight crashes at Yasuko's San Dimas apartment to dodge LB traffic
social_circle.communication_frequency: 3-4x/week (mostly meme exchanges plus one substantive thread)
recent_text_topics: Reminding her — again — to bump her Roth contribution back up now that the January-February crunch is over.
Picking a ramen spot for the May meetup; he's lobbying for Tsujita, she wants somewhere closer to the 605.
Sending port and longshore memes plus a few Dodgers reaction screenshots.
Venting about a recent Long Beach traffic stop that frustrated him; she's the one person he'll talk to about that without filtering.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'My younger brother Daichi is twenty-eight, lives in Long Beach, works in logistics at the port... We share a Spotify family plan... we mostly text memes and meet up for ramen once a month.' Q13: crashes ~twice a year. Q20: rougher police experiences in Long Beach. Q61: 'a small Roth IRA my brother nagged me into opening.' Q83: 'My brother nags me about the Roth.'

social_circle.name: Reyna Delgado

demographics.occupation: Construction foreman (residential remodels) for a mid-sized contractor
demographics.education: High school plus trade certifications; OSHA 30, lead-abatement cert

background.how_they_met: Reyna was Yasuko's foreman for three years on the same contractor's crews before Yasuko moved to Reuben's shop; the working relationship became a real friendship and outlasted the job.
background.why_close: Reyna is Yasuko's main confidante on work stress and the person she calls about jobsite nonsense. She showed up with bibimbap during Yasuko's January 2026 low — 'You don't get to disappear on us, dummy' — which Yasuko explicitly names as the bottom of that stretch. Reyna is also the one openly nagging her to finish the OSHA 30.

interests: coaching her two teenage boys' weekend soccer
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in full sentences with proper punctuation, often profane. Heavy use of voice notes from her truck on the way home from sites. Doesn't really do emoji except an occasional skull or a side-eye. Will call instead of text if it's important.

shared_activities: Phone vents about contractors and clients
Occasional Saturday-morning trail runs when she can sneak away from her boys
Sharing OSHA 30 study materials and quizzing each other
Bail-fund donation matching twice a year
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (mix of texts, voice notes, and short calls)
recent_text_topics: Riding Yasuko about scheduling the OSHA 30 exam before end of summer like she promised.
Updates on a foreman friend's union push at a Glendora site and what Carpenters Local 409 onboarding actually looks like.
Checking in after Yasuko missed a Saturday run — 'don't go quiet on me again.'
Trading jokes about Reuben's disorganization and a specific Sierra Madre client who keeps changing the walnut shelving spec.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07: 'My closest friend is Reyna, a foreman I worked under for three years, she's in her forties and lives in Azusa — she's the person I call when I need to vent about a jobsite.' Q07 follow-up: 'Sites, idiot contractors, her two boys, and whether I should finally take the OSHA test. She's a nag in the best way.' Q30: 'Reyna's been politicized by it — she went to more protests than I did.' Q44: bibimbap intervention, 'You don't get to disappear on us, dummy.' Q49: 'I go to Reyna or Priya.'

social_circle.name: Priya Subramanian

demographics.occupation: Senior graphic designer at an independent branding studio in DTLA
demographics.education: BFA, graphic design (Art Center College of Design, Pasadena)

background.how_they_met: Met at a Tuesday-night figure-drawing session in DTLA; struck up a friendship over a shared distaste for the loud guy at the easel next to them.
background.why_close: Both protect Wednesday mornings against weekend flakiness; Priya is Yasuko's primary creative-conversation partner and one of the only two people (with Reyna) she goes to for emotional support. Priya also referred the Sierra Madre walnut-shelving side gig.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Long, full-sentence iMessages with proper grammar; sometimes a stream of photos of typography or storefronts she sees on walks. Uses tasteful emoji (one heart, one eye-roll). Rarely sends voice notes. Tends to send articles with one line of commentary.

shared_activities: Every-other-Wednesday coffee at Augie's in Pasadena
Occasional weekend gallery visits in DTLA, Culver City, or Chinatown
Sketchbook show-and-tell, exchanging works in progress
Client referrals when one of Priya's branding clients needs custom millwork
recent_text_topics: Confirming whether Wednesday coffee is on or if Priya's deadline will eat it again; rescheduling logistics.
Status updates on the Sierra Madre walnut shelving — the clients have been asking Priya questions she's redirecting to Yasuko.
A Yayoi Kusama show Priya wants to drag her to; trying to find a Saturday that doesn't conflict with a trail run.
A photo Priya sent of a turf-roofed Faroe Islands listing on Airbnb, captioned 'someday fund?'

social_circle.name: Eunhee Park

demographics.occupation: Receptionist at a Korean dental practice in Fullerton; sells homemade banchan informally on the side
demographics.education: Some college in Korea; no degree

background.how_they_met: Yasuko's maternal aunt; stepped in heavily during and after the parents' divorce.
background.why_close: Yasuko describes Eunhee as 'basically a second mom' — taught her proper Korean cooking (including kkakdugi), is the person whose place she crashes at when 'the apartment feels too small for my brain,' and the relationship runs both ways: Yasuko handles Eunhee's taxes and has been more involved since Eunhee's type 2 diabetes diagnosis.

interests: Korean church gossip even though she stopped attending
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Long voice messages in mixed Korean and English; texts often have typos and unintentional autocorrect chaos. Heavy emoji and sticker user. Sends photos of food multiple times a week, sometimes with no caption.

shared_activities: Cooking together (Eunhee teaches, Yasuko writes things down)
Annual tax-prep sessions (Yasuko does it via TurboTax for her)
Occasional overnight stays when Yasuko needs a change of scene
Chuseok and Obon family gatherings
recent_text_topics: Asking Yasuko to double-check the amended 1099 from a side bakery client before she signs it.
Reporting her latest A1C number and what the doctor said about cutting back on rice.
Sending a photo of a fresh batch of kkakdugi with the note 'come pick up before it goes too sour.'
Quietly worrying about Hyejin's stress level and asking Yasuko to keep an eye on her after the fall ER trip.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'an aunt in Fullerton, Eunhee, who's basically a second mom — she's the one who taught me to make proper kkakdugi and who lets me crash at her place when the apartment feels too small for my brain.' Q17: 'I also handle my aunt's taxes — I don't know much but I know more than she does.' Q35: 'My aunt Eunhee has type 2 diabetes she manages reasonably.'
